questions.prompt: A stake is being pulled out of the ground by means of two ropes as shown. Knowing that $\alpha = 30^\circ$, determine by trigonometry the magnitude of the force $\mathbf{P}$ so that the resultant force exerted on the stake is vertical.
questions.solution:
For the resultant $\mathbf{R}$ to be purely vertical, the horizontal components of the two forces must cancel, or equivalently in the closed triangle with vertical $\mathbf{R}$ we apply the law of sines:
$$\frac{P}{\sin 25^\circ} = \frac{120\,\text{N}}{\sin 30^\circ}$$
Solving for $P$:
$$P = (120\,\text{N})\frac{\sin 25^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} = 101.43\,\text{N} \approx 101.4\,\text{N}.$$

questions.prompt: A trolley that moves along a horizontal beam is acted upon by two forces as shown. Knowing that $\alpha = 25^\circ$, determine by trigonometry the magnitude of the force $\mathbf{P}$ so that the resultant force exerted on the trolley is vertical.
questions.solution:
Construct the force triangle with the $1600\text{-N}$ force (at $15^\circ$ below the $-x$ axis, i.e., $75^\circ$ left of the downward vertical), $\mathbf{P}$ (at $\alpha = 25^\circ$ right of the downward vertical), and vertical resultant $\mathbf{R}$. By the law of sines:
$$\frac{P}{\sin 75^\circ} = \frac{1600\,\text{N}}{\sin 25^\circ}$$
Note that $\sin 75^\circ = \cos 15^\circ$, giving:
$$P = (1600\,\text{N})\frac{\cos 15^\circ}{\sin 25^\circ} = 3657\,\text{N} \approx 3660\,\text{N}.$$

questions.prompt: A telephone cable is clamped at $A$ to pole $AB$. Knowing that the tension in the left-hand portion of the cable is $T_1 = 800\,\text{lb}$, determine by trigonometry the required tension $T_2$ in the right-hand portion if the resultant $\mathbf{R}$ of the forces exerted by the cable at $A$ is to be vertical.
questions.solution:
For the resultant $\mathbf{R}$ to be vertical, the horizontal components must cancel (or from the force triangle with interior angles $75^\circ$ and $65^\circ$ adjacent to vertical $\mathbf{R}$):
$$\frac{T_2}{\sin 75^\circ} = \frac{800\,\text{lb}}{\sin 65^\circ} \implies T_2 = 800\,\frac{\cos 15^\circ}{\cos 25^\circ} = 852.6\,\text{lb} \approx 853\,\text{lb}.$$

questions.prompt: Two forces are applied as shown to a hook support. Knowing that the magnitude of $\mathbf{P}$ is $35\,\text{N}$, determine by trigonometry the required angle $\alpha$ (in degrees) if the resultant $\mathbf{R}$ of the two forces applied to the support is to be horizontal.
questions.solution:
In the force triangle with horizontal resultant $\mathbf{R}$, the angle opposite $\mathbf{P}$ is $25^\circ$ and the angle opposite the $50\text{-N}$ force is $\alpha$. By the law of sines (or $\sum F_y = 0$):
$$\frac{35\,\text{N}}{\sin 25^\circ} = \frac{50\,\text{N}}{\sin\alpha} \implies \sin\alpha = \frac{50\sin 25^\circ}{35} = 0.60374 \implies \alpha = 37.14^\circ \approx 37.1^\circ.$$

questions.prompt: A steel tank is to be positioned in an excavation. Knowing that $\alpha = 20^\circ$, determine by trigonometry the required magnitude of the force $\mathbf{P}$ if the resultant $\mathbf{R}$ of the two forces applied at $A$ is to be vertical.
questions.solution:
The $425\text{-lb}$ force makes $60^\circ$ with the upward vertical and $\mathbf{P}$ makes $90^\circ - 20^\circ = 70^\circ$ with the upward vertical. By the law of sines on the closed triangle with vertical resultant $\mathbf{R}$:
$$\frac{P}{\sin 60^\circ} = \frac{425\,\text{lb}}{\sin 70^\circ} \implies P = 425\,\frac{\cos 30^\circ}{\cos 20^\circ} = 391.7\,\text{lb} \approx 392\,\text{lb}.$$

questions.prompt: The hydraulic cylinder $BD$ exerts on member $ABC$ a force $\mathbf{P}$ directed along line $BD$. Knowing that $\mathbf{P}$ must have a $750\text{-N}$ component perpendicular to member $ABC$, determine the magnitude of the force $\mathbf{P}$.
questions.solution:
Member $ABC$ forms $60^\circ$ with the vertical wall (i.e., $30^\circ$ above the horizontal), while cylinder $BD$ forms $50^\circ$ with the horizontal. Therefore, the acute angle between $\mathbf{P}$ (along $BD$) and member $ABC$ is $\theta = 50^\circ - 30^\circ = 20^\circ$. Since the component perpendicular to $ABC$ is $P\sin 20^\circ = 750\,\text{N}$:
$$P = \frac{750\,\text{N}}{\sin 20^\circ} = 2192.9\,\text{N} \approx 2190\,\text{N}.$$

questions.prompt: Cable $AC$ exerts on beam $AB$ a force $\mathbf{P}$ directed along line $AC$. Knowing that $\mathbf{P}$ must have a $350\text{-lb}$ vertical component, determine the magnitude of the force $\mathbf{P}$.
questions.solution:
Cable $AC$ forms an angle of $55^\circ$ with the vertical wall at $C$, so the vertical component of $\mathbf{P}$ is $P_y = P\cos 55^\circ$. Setting $P_y = 350\,\text{lb}$:
$$P = \frac{350\,\text{lb}}{\cos 55^\circ} = 610.2\,\text{lb} \approx 610\,\text{lb}.$$

questions.prompt: Determine the magnitude and direction of the resultant of the three forces shown ($800\,\text{N}$, $424\,\text{N}$, and $408\,\text{N}$) using rectangular components.
questions.solution:
Compute the lengths of the three dimension triangles:
- $800\,\text{N}$: $d_1 = \sqrt{800^2 + 600^2} = 1000\,\text{mm} \implies F_{1x} = +640\,\text{N},\; F_{1y} = +480\,\text{N}$.
- $424\,\text{N}$: $d_2 = \sqrt{560^2 + 900^2} = 1060\,\text{mm} \implies F_{2x} = -424\left(\frac{560}{1060}\right) = -224\,\text{N},\; F_{2y} = -424\left(\frac{900}{1060}\right) = -360\,\text{N}$.
- $408\,\text{N}$: $d_3 = \sqrt{480^2 + 900^2} = 1020\,\text{mm} \implies F_{3x} = +408\left(\frac{480}{1020}\right) = +192\,\text{N},\; F_{3y} = -408\left(\frac{900}{1020}\right) = -360\,\text{N}$.

Sum components: $R_x = 640 - 224 + 192 = +608\,\text{N}$, $R_y = 480 - 360 - 360 = -240\,\text{N}$. Thus $R = \sqrt{608^2 + (-240)^2} = 653.6\,\text{N} \approx 654\,\text{N}$ and $\tan\alpha = 240/608 \implies \alpha = 21.5^\circ$ below the $+x$ axis.

questions.prompt: Knowing that $\alpha = 35^\circ$, determine the resultant of the three forces acting on the collar shown.
questions.solution:
Resolve each force into horizontal and vertical components ($\alpha = 35^\circ$, and the $150\text{-N}$ force is at $35^\circ + 30^\circ = 65^\circ$ below $+x$):
$$R_x = -200\cos 35^\circ + 150\cos 65^\circ + 100\cos 35^\circ = -18.52\,\text{N}$$
$$R_y = -200\sin 35^\circ - 150\sin 65^\circ - 100\sin 35^\circ = -308.02\,\text{N}$$
Hence $R = \sqrt{(-18.52)^2 + (-308.02)^2} = 308.6\,\text{N} \approx 309\,\text{N}$, and $\theta = \tan^{-1}(308.02 / 18.52) = 86.6^\circ$ below the $-x$ axis.

questions.prompt: Two cables are tied together at $C$ and support a $1600\text{-kg}$ mass as shown. Determine the tension in cable $AC$ (in $\text{kN}$).
questions.solution:
Weight of the load is $W = (1600\,\text{kg})(9.81\,\text{m/s}^2) = 15.696\,\text{kN}$. Cable lengths are $AC = \sqrt{1100^2 + 960^2} = 1460\,\text{mm}$ and $BC = \sqrt{400^2 + 960^2} = 1040\,\text{mm}$. Equilibrium of joint $C$:
$$\sum F_x = -T_{AC}\left(\frac{1100}{1460}\right) + T_{BC}\left(\frac{400}{1040}\right) = 0 \implies T_{BC} = 1.9589\,T_{AC}$$
$$\sum F_y = T_{AC}\left(\frac{960}{1460}\right) + T_{BC}\left(\frac{960}{1040}\right) - 15.696 = 0$$
Substituting $T_{BC}$ gives $(0.6575 + 1.8082)T_{AC} = 15.696 \implies T_{AC} = 6.366\,\text{kN} \approx 6.37\,\text{kN}$.

questions.prompt: Two cables are tied together at $C$ and are loaded as shown. Knowing that $P = 500\,\text{N}$ and $\alpha = 60^\circ$, determine the tension in cable $BC$.
questions.solution:
Resolve the equilibrium equations for joint $C$: $\sum F_x = -T_{AC}\cos 45^\circ + T_{BC}\cos 25^\circ - 500\cos 60^\circ = 0$ and $\sum F_y = T_{AC}\sin 45^\circ + T_{BC}\sin 25^\circ - 500\sin 60^\circ = 0$. Adding the two equations eliminates $T_{AC}$:
$$T_{BC}(\cos 25^\circ + \sin 25^\circ) = 500(\cos 60^\circ + \sin 60^\circ) \implies 1.3289\,T_{BC} = 683.01 \implies T_{BC} = 513.96\,\text{N} \approx 514\,\text{N}.$$

questions.prompt: A sailor is being rescued using a boatswain's chair suspended from a pulley that can roll freely on support cable $ACB$ and is pulled at constant speed by traction cable $CD$. Knowing that $\alpha = 30^\circ$, $\beta = 10^\circ$, and the combined weight of chair and sailor is $900\,\text{N}$, determine the tension in the support cable $ACB$.
questions.solution:
Because the pulley rolls freely on cable $ACB$, the tension $T$ is identical in segments $CA$ and $CB$. Equilibrium of the pulley at $C$ (with $T_{CD}$ along the $30^\circ$ direction of $CA$):
$$\sum F_x = -(T + T_{CD})\cos 30^\circ + T\cos 10^\circ = 0 \implies T_{CD} = T\left(\frac{\cos 10^\circ}{\cos 30^\circ} - 1\right) = 0.13715\,T$$
$$\sum F_y = (T + T_{CD})\sin 30^\circ + T\sin 10^\circ - 900 = 0$$
Substituting $T_{CD}$:
$$T(1.13715\sin 30^\circ + \sin 10^\circ) = 900 \implies 0.74222\,T = 900 \implies T = 1212.6\,\text{N} \approx 1213\,\text{N}.$$

questions.prompt: Two forces $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ are applied as shown to an aircraft connection. Knowing that the connection is in equilibrium and that $P = 500\,\text{lb}$ and $Q = 650\,\text{lb}$, determine the magnitudes of the forces exerted on rods $A$ and $B$.
questions.solution:
Write the equilibrium equations for the pin:
$$\sum F_y = F_A\sin 50^\circ - 500\,\text{lb} - (650\,\text{lb})\cos 40^\circ = 0 \implies F_A = \frac{500 + 497.93}{\sin 50^\circ} = 1302.7\,\text{lb} \approx 1303\,\text{lb}.$$
$$\sum F_x = -F_A\cos 50^\circ - F_B + (650\,\text{lb})\sin 40^\circ = 0 \implies F_B = 417.81 - 1302.7\cos 50^\circ = -419.6\,\text{lb}.$$
The negative sign means $\mathbf{F}_B$ acts to the right (compression), with magnitude $F_B = 420\,\text{lb}$.

questions.prompt: Determine the Cartesian vector representation $(F_x\mathbf{i} + F_y\mathbf{j} + F_z\mathbf{k})$ of the $900\text{-N}$ force shown in space.
questions.solution:
The $900\text{-N}$ force forms $65^\circ$ with the horizontal $xz$ plane (so $\theta_y = 90^\circ - 65^\circ = 25^\circ$):
$$F_y = +(900\,\text{N})\sin 65^\circ = +815.7\,\text{N} \approx +816\,\text{N}, \qquad F_h = (900\,\text{N})\cos 65^\circ = 380.36\,\text{N}.$$
In the $xz$ plane, $F_h$ is directed $20^\circ$ from the $+z$ axis toward the $-x$ axis:
$$F_x = -F_h\sin 20^\circ = -130.1\,\text{N}, \qquad F_z = +F_h\cos 20^\circ = +357.4\,\text{N} \approx +357\,\text{N}.$$

questions.prompt: Three cables are used to tether a balloon as shown. Determine the vertical force $P$ exerted by the balloon at $A$ knowing that the tension in cable $AD$ is $481\,\text{N}$.
questions.solution:
From $A(0, 5.60, 0)\,\text{m}$ to the anchors: $\overrightarrow{AB} = -4.20\mathbf{i} - 5.60\mathbf{j}\,\text{m}$ ($d_{AB} = 7.00\,\text{m}$), $\overrightarrow{AC} = 2.40\mathbf{i} - 5.60\mathbf{j} + 4.20\mathbf{k}\,\text{m}$ ($d_{AC} = 7.40\,\text{m}$), and $\overrightarrow{AD} = -5.60\mathbf{j} - 3.30\mathbf{k}\,\text{m}$ ($d_{AD} = 6.50\,\text{m}$).
With $T_{AD} = 481\,\text{N}$, $\dfrac{T_{AD}}{d_{AD}} = \dfrac{481}{6.50} = 74\,\text{N/m}$, so $\mathbf{T}_{AD} = (-414.4\,\text{N})\mathbf{j} - (244.2\,\text{N})\mathbf{k}$.
From $\sum F_z = 0$: $-244.2 + T_{AC}\left(\frac{4.20}{7.40}\right) = 0 \implies \frac{T_{AC}}{7.40} = 58.143\,\text{N/m}$.
From $\sum F_x = 0$: $58.143(2.40) - T_{AB}\left(\frac{4.20}{7.00}\right) = 0 \implies \frac{T_{AB}}{7.00} = 33.224\,\text{N/m}$.
From $\sum F_y = 0$: $P = 414.4 + 58.143(5.60) + 33.224(5.60) = 926.1\,\text{N} \approx 926\,\text{N}$.

questions.prompt: Collars $A$ and $B$ are connected by a $525\text{-mm}$-long wire and can slide freely on frictionless rods. If a force $\mathbf{P} = (341\,\text{N})\mathbf{j}$ is applied to collar $A$, determine the tension in the wire when $y = 155\,\text{mm}$.
questions.solution:
Collar $A$ lies at $(0, 155, 0)\,\text{mm}$ and collar $B$ lies at $(200, 0, z)\,\text{mm}$, so the wire vector from $A$ to $B$ is $\overrightarrow{AB} = 200\mathbf{i} - 155\mathbf{j} + z\mathbf{k}\,\text{mm}$ with length $d = 525\,\text{mm}$. For collar $A$ sliding on the frictionless vertical $y$ rod, the normal reaction of the rod has zero $y$ component. Thus $\sum F_y = 0$ on collar $A$ gives:
$$341 - T\left(\frac{155}{525}\right) = 0 \implies T = 341\left(\frac{525}{155}\right) = 1155\,\text{N}.$$
